question: If both arms encounter the same first-program TypeError, does showing the failing source in the repair message improve independent file score by t=395 s?

source.transformation: Strip all Python COMMENT tokens in both arms, preserving source line numbers and AST. The original model output included an explicit self-diagnosis in an inline comment. Keep that annotation and the reference correction out of both prompts. Use the exact resulting controlled_source_sha256.

timing.start: t=0 is the start of each fresh 720-second task session after equal server warm-up. On the otherwise identical first provider request, a scripted provider returns the common fixed text program at monotonic t=250 s, then all later inference uses the common pinned live model. No repair request may begin before t=250 s.
timing.measure: Log actual first-program release, nonzero execution, dispatch of the repair request and snapshot offsets. Allow at most 2 s release jitter and 5 s from release to repair dispatch in both arms; otherwise record an infrastructure gap and rerun the pair. Both arms receive approximately 145 s to repair, including execution/dispatch overhead. Score frozen deliverables once, independently, at t=395 s.

split.unit: Two new input sets reproduce the same fixed defect; this diagnoses conditional repair and cannot estimate natural end-to-end score.

design.candidate: text-source with only ±2 lines of the failing common first program appended, at most 800 characters
design.shared_state: Identical task, inputs, first outbound prompt, scripted first reply and sandbox wrapper/traceback. Fresh workspaces and independent model-server processes; same model warm-up; send only standard task inputs and arm-appropriate derived feedback. Never supply the positive control, future output files, full source, reference costs or this host protocol to the repair model.
design.settings: Use the fixed_settings from the inherited repair-source-v1 protocol, except for the explicitly scripted shared first response and timing above. Pair each of 3 executions on the same hosted CPU per input with fresh model processes and workspaces.
design.evaluation: Primary grade normalized delivery score at t=395 s. Report all six paired scores, per-case and per-repeat case-macro paired changes, mean and sample variance with n-1 across the 3 repeats, completed-repair-response count and actual exposures. Grade missing files at a valid stable cutoff zero; replay/infra/cutoff failures unmeasured.
design.decision: Six complete pairs; all 6 candidate repair requests must demonstrably contain the correctly sourced excerpt and all 6 baseline repair requests must lack it. If any pair, dispatch, or exposure check is incomplete, report insufficient evidence. With complete coverage, proceed to a naturally failing task family only if all 3 repeat-level macro differences are strictly positive and neither input has a negative mean paired difference. Otherwise stop this candidate and retain the existing text policy. This measures recovery conditional on the same induced failure.
design.attempts: Keep every original attempt, recording reason, run and timestamp. Re-run an entire pair only on technical failure, never for a low score. Preserve the first valid paired execution for analysis.

inherits.implementation_lock: Before dispatch, commit the runner, scripted first response, pristine-case preparation and host-only scorer to one immutable experiment SHA. Record the SHA, run ID and job IDs. Replay one positive and negative control through the production wrapper before starting inference.
